thread:
alex: Handoff from day shift. Ongoing high request rate against /v1/generate for model-west-1 (redwood-gpt-13b). Alerting since ~09:12 UTC, sustained error budget burn. Primary: alex (finishing), Secondary: mira (taking). Summary below.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] rate_spike_high - /v1/generate - triggers: 1200 rps sustained over 5m - pager: page_7832 - severity: P2

alex: Impact: increase in 5xxs (mostly 504 gateway timeout) and request queuing. Customer-facing: some customers on Dedicated reporting slow responses; Hosted is degraded for extra-long prompts (>2048 tokens). No total outage.

alex: Mitigations started: 1) Enabled fallback routing to model-east-1 variant (latency bump but lower queue). 2) Increased autoscale max replicas on gpu-pool-gen-west by +30%. 3) Temporarily reduced max_sequence_length to 4096 -> 3072 for non-enterprise customers (config push).

alex: Commands run (logs attached):
```bash
# bump autoscale max
redwood infra pool update gpu-pool-gen-west --max-replicas 80
# rollout config change
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/generator MAX_SEQ=3072 --record
```

mira: I'm taking over as secondary. I'll confirm the autoscale change finished and monitor queues/latency for 30m. Ryan, can you watch routing metrics and confirm the fallback remains stable?

ryan: On it. I've already opened a tracing span to correlate 504s to specific instance types. Early signal: g4dn instances are hitting IO stall during KV cache write. DigiOps flagged NVMe utilization rising.

infra-sre-bot: [TASK] Autoscale change completed for gpu-pool-gen-west at 09:28 UTC. New max replicas: 80.

mira: Thanks. Next steps I'm doing now: - Verify prefix/KV cache health - Check Nginx fronting timeouts (maybe tune keepalive) - Watch worker OOM / swap. If IO persists, plan is to divert some traffic to quantized-variants (lower memory) for non-enterprise customers.

sophia: FYI product: Ticket queue shows 4 customer reports mentioning big slowdowns (CustomerA, CustomerB, CustomerC, internal test org). No SLA breaches yet but warning. I've created a customer incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/RED-7832

alex: Runbook refs: - Rate Spike playbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rate-spike
- Routing fallback doc: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/routing-fallback
- KV cache recovery: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-restart

Note: When diverting to quantized variants, use routing tag `fallback-quant` and only enable for guests + non-enterprise tenants. See snippet below:
```json
{"route_policy": "fallback-quant", "match": {"customer_tier": ["guest","standard"]}}
```

mira: Doing a dry-run of divert for 10% of traffic to quantized model now. Will report metrics in 5m.

oncall-bot: [AUDIT] traffic-diversion job started by mira (10%) at 09:33 UTC. Job id: td_9921

ryan: Early read: tail latency for quantized route looks stable, error rate drops by ~30% for diverted traffic. Backend IO on g4dn still high but overall queue depth decreased ~18%.

mira: Good. I'll roll to 30% after confirming no regressions in output quality for tracked prompts. Alex — any service-level changes I should be aware of for the handoff?

alex: Nothing else. Note coverage gap 11:15–11:45 UTC: scheduled org sync means I won't be available for that slot. Mira you will be primary then — can you confirm coverage? If not, @sophia please cover notifications for customer comms.

mira: I can cover 11:15–11:45. I'll stay on pager for that window.

sophia: I'll prepare a short customer update template if we need to notify enterprise customers — draft in #customer-success later.

ryan: Observability checklist for next shift: - confirm autoscale settled - check NVMe utilization per instance - review KV cache error logs and restart slow shards if needed (runbook above).

mira: Actions for night team / next shift: 1) If 5xx rate > 5% for >15m escalate to P1 and call infra oncall. 2) If IO persists after divert to quantized at 50%, consider degrading long prompts for hosted customers (config gating) and notify product. 3) Hold on full pool restart unless KV cache runbook suggests it — avoid simultaneous restarts during high load.

alex: Accepting handoff. Mira is primary, Ryan is secondary for infra metrics, Sophia handles CS comms. Leaving detailed logs + commands in incident doc.

mira: Taking over. I'll post periodic updates every 15m or on significant changes. Current status: mitigations active, customer impact moderate (some increased latency + timeouts for heavy prompts), no data loss.

oncall-bot: [REMINDER] Please post your acceptance with `+ack` to confirm takeover.

mira: +ack

alex: Thanks, team. Leaving now. Good luck. :v:
